A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AFedPG research. Their main text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original MuJoCo reward and training-time experiments in Figures 3–4 and computation-heterogeneity results in Figure 6.

after.justification: v4 retains those experiments and adds communication-overhead results in Figure 7 and longer-training results in Figure 8.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 revise the distributed update procedure. In v3, agents compute lookahead parameters and momentum directions and transmit directions. In v4, agents transmit gradient estimates; the server maintains the direction recursion using its previous update direction and computes and transmits lookahead parameters. The basic normalized-update and lookahead ingredients remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Swimmer-v4, Hopper-v4, Walker2D-v4, and Humanoid-v4 and retain the same computing-heterogeneity scenarios. Communication measurements and longer training use this existing coverage; the newly discussed noncommunicating-agent case is not a new experiment.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain single-agent PG, synchronous FedPG, A3C, and the vanilla variant without delay-adaptive lookahead. Figures 7–8 reuse FedPG and PG. Newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 adds supplementary protocols: Figure 8 uses five times Figure 3's sample budgets, and Figure 7 measures transmitted bytes with eight agents on Swimmer-v4, including a server window corresponding to one synchronous round. The original experimental settings and Table 3 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds two substantive analyses: communication-load distribution across agents and server time steps, and longer training to examine eventual rewards versus convergence speed. These extend the retained lookahead ablation and computation-heterogeneity analysis.

E5.justification: The added Figure 8 reports five independent runs with seeds 0–4 and 95% confidence intervals. The original results retain ten runs with seeds 0–9 and 95% intervals. This adds a different repetition count for the supplementary experiment, without reducing repetitions for the original comparisons.

E6.justification: Figures 3, 4, and 6 retain their results. New Figure 7 reports similar cumulative communication volumes but different agent allocation and smoother server traffic. Figure 8 adds longer-training curves showing broadly similar eventual rewards across AFedPG agent counts, with faster attainment using more agents and a remaining Humanoid PG deficit. These are additional results under extended settings.

T1.justification: v4 adds the explicit Fisher-matrix lower-bound assumption B.3 and substantially revises and expands the error-recursion and delay-bound derivations. It also introduces fixed-runtime reasoning and uses a delay condition in Equation 38. The FOSP theorem changes from a last-iterate bound with a bias floor to a weighted-average, bias-free statement, aligning it with the result already targeted in v3 Appendix B.5.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: asynchronous policy-gradient learning with delay-adaptive lookahead, convergence guarantees, linear per-agent sample-complexity improvement, and reduced training time. The revised theorem details do not change these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of communication-load redistribution and interprets longer training as achieving similar rewards faster. It acknowledges suboptimal PG hyperparameters on Humanoid and explicitly discusses noncommunicating stragglers. Section 7.1 removes the limited-agent-scale caveat without adding a larger-agent experiment.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly specifies float32 parameter representation for communication accounting and describes the agent/server measurement setup. The existing MLP architectures, learning rates, GAE setting, PyTorch implementation, and A100 hardware information remain unchanged; no new code-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v4 adds references including Fu, Gaur, Wang (2024a), Xiong, Zheng, and Zhu. New Appendix C.1 substantially expands positioning against Shen et al. (2023), contrasting algorithm class, function parameterization, convergence complexity, and delay assumptions. The original FL/FedRL discussion is retained as C.2.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence largely remain. v4 reverses the presentation order of the global and FOSP theorems, retitles appendix sections, adds roadmap and proof-explanation prose, and moves the existing C.1 discussion to C.2. These are localized structural and language changes.

P2.justification: v4 adds the two-panel communication Figure 7 and four-panel longer-training Figure 8, reformats the algorithm boxes, and relocates existing figures and tables through page reflow. The original result plots and Tables 1–3 retain their content and visual design.

improvement.justification: v4 improves empirical interpretation through communication measurements and longer-training evidence, and aligns the FOSP statement with its appendix proof while making the Fisher assumption explicit. The gain is limited by remaining inconsistencies: global Theorem 5.1 still omits the new B.3 assumption used by its supporting lemma, and the scale limitation is removed without a larger-agent experiment.
